read_this_first.headline: The cheapest correct move is almost certainly to delete NOTHING from inside refer-zo-bootstrap, and instead retire the directory as one unit.
why: It is a SEPARATE GIT REPOSITORY. E:/refer-script-factory/refer-zo-bootstrap has its own .git, its own remote (github.com/lightedcandle/refer-zo-bootstrap.git), 343 tracked files, and it is fully pushed on branch build-out-hive - 0 ahead, 0 behind. Everything proposed for deletion below already exists on GitHub.

It is INVISIBLE TO THE FACTORY REPO'S GIT. `git ls-files refer-zo-bootstrap` in E:/refer-script-factory returns zero. The directory is excluded by .git/info/exclude line 7 - a local, uncommitted exclude, not in .gitignore and not present in any clone. So deleting files here removes nothing from the factory repo's history, because nothing was ever in it.

Picking files out costs more than it saves. Every candidate below has live callers INSIDE that same directory, chiefly its own `npm run check` (package.json line 12) which node --checks all of them in one command. Removing any one file turns that check red in a repo whose whole remaining value is being a readable historical record.

The savings are nil. This is roughly 100KB of .mjs in a directory nobody imports from the factory repo's own source. Deleting it frees nothing and risks a working tree going dirty in a repo no session is watching.
read_this_first.recommended_instead: Mark the directory retired with a README at its root pointing at .refer-factory/zo-method-harvest.json, and leave the files. If the operator wants the disk back later, remove the WHOLE directory in one action - origin has it - rather than pruning inside it. That is one reversible action with one caller set to fix, instead of twelve.

THE ONLY SURVIVING PROOF OF WHAT EVER ACTUALLY RAN, and it is gitignored - it exists on this disk and nowhere else. heartbeat.log is four lines and heartbeat-state.json shows the hive heartbeat running with unsubstituted <NODE_ID> placeholders and hive_status skipped for no_hive_url. That is the evidence that separates 'ran and failed' from 'never ran', which is the distinction this whole retirement turned on. Losing it is unrecoverable.

Already the standing recommendation on the belt, from finding hive-registry-is-fed-for-one-node-of-four: 'a registry that forgets a node it once had cannot tell you the node stopped, which is the one thing it exists to say.' All four rows were retired by marking.
